description:
FILED s484d (2026-09-14).  t/op/fork.t produced 1 row until this session
(#1652); it now runs all 28 of perl's, 20 passing.  The 8 failures are all
"the mechanism runs, the output differs" (scratch/s484d/keep-cons/
op_fork.t.out), records 2, 14, 15, 16, 22, 25, 27 plus one row with no GOT:

  * two records print `parent died at - line 10.` / `at - line 1.` where perl
    prints the child's output first -- the parent's `die` wins a race PCL
    orders differently;
  * one prints `child: called as [main::f()]` where perl prints a different
    caller rendering;
  * the rest are one-line output-order or value differences.
NOT attributed further: each needs its record read against perl's.  The
docs/not-supported.md `fork` caveats are the first thing to check -- a
fork-then-continue child is an SBCL process, so `$? & 127` reads 0 where perl
shows the signal number.

SECOND FINDING, A REPORTING BUG (no rows behind it, but it will cost a
session): the file's snapshot row now carries
`sig = crash:sb-sys:interactive-interrupt` and **the file did not crash** --
it ran to `1..28`.  The text is a RECORD PROGRAM's own diagnostic, quoted
inside a TAP comment: the record at t/op/fork.t line 70 does `kill 'INT',
$cid`, its PCL child takes the SIGINT, and run_multiple_progs prints the
child's output in its `# GOT:` block.  `tools/run-perl-suite.pl`'s signature
scan (`$sig ||= "crash:$1" if $pcl =~ ...`) reads the whole captured stream
and does not skip `#` comment lines, so a quoted crash becomes the FILE's
crash.  A one-line fix (ignore lines beginning with `#` in that scan) would
change the sig of every file whose diagnostics quote such text, several of
them blessed in baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv, so it owes a
before/after of the whole companion population -- which is why it is filed
and not done here.
subject: op/fork.t's 8 rows -- PCL's fork runs the records but the child's exit/signal reporting differs; and the file's `sig` is a FALSE crash report
